title: Use the subtraction law of logs to turn a sum of logs of ratios into a telescoping sum
content: A sum such as Sum log_a((n+2)/(n+1)) can be split, using the subtraction law log(p/q) = log(p) - log(q), into (log_a(3) + log_a(4) + ... + log_a(50)) - (log_a(2) + log_a(3) + ... + log_a(49)). Writing out the first few and last few terms of each bracket shows that almost every term cancels (telescopes), leaving only the first term of the second bracket and the last term of the first bracket. The sum then collapses to log_a(last term of first bracket) - log_a(first term of second bracket), which can be simplified using the subtraction law again into a single log of a ratio.
